Synopsis:
An aging expeditioner gives the player the task of collecting a githyanki egg and debates nature vs. nurture.

Cluster Contexts:
- CRE_Expeditioner.json: You and your party are approaching a githyanki crèche on a rocky roof (there’s also a skittish bird guarding a nest of baked goods nearby), when an aging expeditioner, Lady Esther, stops you. She claims the Society of Brilliance commissioned her to procure a githyanki egg so they can incubate and raise the hatchling in a peaceful tradition, but she was chased and insulted when she tried to buy one and is still indignant about it. The conversation centers on whether a githyanki’s violence is innate or taught—Lady Esther is contemptuous of the Society’s optimism, while the player may argue nurture and Lae’zel vehemently opposes stealing any gith child. Lady Esther asks the player to help infiltrate the crèche and acquire an egg, promising reward if you succeed.
- CRE_MonasteryApproach_Bird_SWA.json: You find a blue jay perched in a makeshift nest while climbing the mountain toward the gith creche; larger eagles have taken over the roof and repeatedly steal nests, prey and territory. Off-screen the eagles occupy the roof as a prime lookout (they even prey on the “drunk lizards” the jay mentions), and the jay bitterly longs for its original nest up there. The bird is scared and desperate—it will plead with the player to drive off or kill the eagles, but can also react if the player refuses. Note: the jay’s nest (or what it leaves behind if startled) contains baked goods, a potential loot outcome if the bird is scared away.
- CRE_Hatchery_Caretaker.json: The gith caretaker asks what the player is doing in the hatchery. They can learn some interesting lore about githyanki eggs. The player can also convince the caretaker to give them the last unhatched egg - but he is quite attached to it.
- GOB_Checkpoint_Guard001.json: All guards at the checkpoint point the player to the guard with this dialog. He is an evil, nasty character who has no reason to go easy on the player. Should ooze disdain. This is the first goblin we meet and their weasly, cruel, wicked nature should stand out.
The goblin will let a non-allied player in only if they smear worg shit on their face. Yuck.
- NGB_FOR_Village_Trespassing.json: This guard has come upon you sneaking through a village her force is occupying. She was bored and sees you as a potential source of fun (ie, someone to murder/bully).  Defaulting to she, but numerous goblins could deliver this dialogue as it's a dynamic crime one.

context: You and your party are approaching a rocky rooftop where a githyanki crèche sits in the distance; a skittish blue jay with a stash of baked goods and territorial eagles occupy the approach. An aging expeditioner, Lady Esther, claims the Society of Brilliance commissioned her to procure a githyanki egg so the Society can incubate and raise the hatchling peacefully; she says gith tried to chase and insult her when she attempted to acquire one. Esther is contemptuous of the Society’s optimism and argues githyanki violence is innate, while the player may argue nurture. Lae’zel is present and vehemently opposes stealing any gith child, threatening violence at the suggestion. Off-screen the hatchery’s caretaker is attached to the last unhatched egg—Esther asks the player to infiltrate the crèche and promises a reward if they bring her an egg.
